title: Pin template dependencies + add vulnerability scanning workflows
author: Sahana Iyer
release_notes: Templates now pin dependencies by default and run scheduled + PR-time vulnerability scans (pip-audit/OSV for Python; npm audit/OSV for TS). Maintainers should follow docs/dependency-upgrades.md for safe upgrades and regenerating lockfiles.
description: Summary: This PR locks down dependency versions across the Python and TypeScript quickstart templates, adds automated vulnerability scanning in CI (PR-time + scheduled), and documents the upgrade process for template maintainers to reduce supply-chain risk. Motivation: Security review flagged unpinned transitive dependencies and lack of automated scanning (see ENG-4190 and template security review open items). We also want template repos to adhere to the Secure SDLC addendum for templates (dependency pinning, vulnerability scanning, and a repeatable upgrade story) without introducing noisy/flake-prone CI failures. Changes included: (1) Python template: move to fully pinned requirements (direct + transitive) via pip-tools, commit compiled requirements with hashes, and add a make target to regenerate; (2) TypeScript template: ensure package-lock.json is committed and consistent, add npm overrides for known vulnerable transitive packages where upstream hasn’t released yet; (3) CI: add a security scanning workflow that runs pip-audit + osv-scanner for Python and npm audit + osv-scanner for TS, with a nightly schedule and a lightweight PR check; (4) Docs: add docs/dependency-upgrades.md describing the approved upgrade cadence, how to regenerate lockfiles, how to handle false positives, and how to record remediation notes. Operational notes: The PR-time workflow is configured to avoid high-noise findings (dev-only packages in example tooling) and to fail only on high/critical CVEs by default; nightly runs are stricter and open an issue with a report artifact. Checklist: - [x] Pin Python deps with hashes - [x] Commit package-lock and align npm ci in CI - [x] Add vuln scanning workflow (PR + schedule) - [x] Document upgrade process + remediation guidelines - [x] Verify templates still install on macOS/Linux (python 3.11, node 20) - [x] No secrets in repo / no new external service tokens. Rollout: This is repo-only and should not impact Redwood API behavior. If CI noise is higher than expected, we can adjust severity thresholds or add targeted ignores with justification in docs/dependency-upgrades.md (no blanket allowlists).
commits: chore(python): compile and pin template requirements with hashes
chore(ts): commit package-lock and normalize npm ci usage
ci(security): add pip-audit + npm audit + osv-scanner workflows (PR + nightly)
docs: add dependency upgrade + remediation guide for maintainers
chore: add make/npm scripts for lockfile regeneration
conversation: Monica Patel (review): Love the direction. Two nits: (1) can we avoid pinning a pre-release for numpy/scipy equivalents if we don’t need them? (2) please ensure the template README still works with `pip install -r requirements.txt` without requiring pip-tools locally.

Sahana Iyer (author): Ack. Dropped the pre-release pin; the compiled set now stays on stable releases. README flow unchanged; pip-tools is only required for maintainers when regenerating via `make deps-update`.

Marcus Lin (review): For the scanning workflow, please avoid adding broad allowlists. If we need ignores, require a short justification + expiration date. Also: make sure scans run on forks without requiring secrets.

Sahana Iyer (author): Updated docs/dependency-upgrades.md with an ignore policy section (justification + expiry) and confirmed workflows use only GitHub-provided token permissions. Forks run PR checks without secrets; nightly issue creation is skipped on forks.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Please confirm we’re not printing env vars or token-like strings in scan output artifacts. Some tools dump environment context by default.

Sahana Iyer (author): Good catch—set `PIP_AUDIT_FORMAT=json` and upload only the JSON report; also redacted workflow step logs by default (no `set -x`). Added a note in SECURITY.md about artifact contents.
Christine Wong (review): Severity gating looks reasonable. Can we add a small note on what happens when nightly finds a vuln (who is on-call / how we triage)?

Sahana Iyer (author): Added a short triage section pointing to the DevEx rotation and linking ENG-4190 for remediation tracking; nightly workflow opens an issue with label `security` + `dependencies`.
Monica Patel (approval): Approved after latest changes. Thanks for adding the maintainers guide—this will reduce churn.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved. Please keep the ignore mechanism strict as documented.
